content:
The multistate salmonella outbreak linked to raw oysters from Virginia's Little Wicomico River is bigger than federal officials first reported — and every oyster sample pulled from the river has now tested positive, according to state and federal updates published Oct. 21–23.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention posted its first notice on Oct. 19: 27 people sick with Salmonella in 12 states, five of 21 with information hospitalized, no deaths, with illnesses beginning May 29 through Sept. 14. Ten of the sick people reported eating raw oysters, and traceback for seven of ten ran to the Little Wicomico Oyster Company on Virginia's Little Wicomico River.

The Food and Drug Administration's safety alert the same day named the serotype, Telelkebir, the dealer certification VA-1421-SP, and a harvest window of Sept. 18 to Oct. 8, with distribution to 15 states and the District of Columbia. On Oct. 9, the company voluntarily recalled whole shellstock oysters harvested from the Little Wicomico River and Little Wicomico River Lower growing areas in that window, and ceased harvesting in the affected area.

Virginia's own count is much higher: its tally, posted Oct. 21, was 55 sick in 19 states, with the newest illness beginning Oct. 6 — inside the recalled harvest window. On Oct. 23, the Virginia Department of Health added the result that matters most: all eight oyster meat samples from the 400 oysters it pulled from river cages on Oct. 13 tested positive for Salmonella. The river was closed Oct. 9 for an initial 30 days and reopens only after three consecutive negative rounds; the emergency condemnation order keeps the downstream portion closed through Nov. 7.

The two counts have not been publicly reconciled: the CDC's 27 cases all began before the recall window, while Virginia's count includes illnesses beginning inside it. Webb Watch is reporting both figures with their sources rather than presenting either as the single total.

Officials emphasize that oysters harvested from other Virginia growing waters are not included in the recall. The FDA advises the public not to eat, sell, or serve the recalled oysters, and to discard or return them. This story updates Webb Watch's Oct. 21 report on the oyster recall with the new Virginia figures, the sample results, and the closure timeline.

Sources:

  • CDC, Salmonella outbreak linked to raw oysters, first notice Oct. 19, 2026
  • FDA, Safety alert: Salmonella in oysters from the Little Wicomico River, Virginia, Oct. 19, 2026
  • Virginia Department of Health, emergency condemnation order, Little Wicomico River
  • Virginia Department of Health tally and sample results, Oct. 21–23, 2026, as reported Oct. 24–25

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Virginia now counts 55 illnesses in the raw-oyster salmonella outbreak — more than double the CDC's 27 — and all eight oyster samples from the Little Wicomico River tested positive.
title: Oyster salmonella count climbs: Virginia reports 55 illnesses as all river samples test positive
